phase_1_task.objective: Build and prove a strict-wrapped pointing scorer. Nothing else.
phase_1_task.why_this_first: It is the gate on every downstream decision in this lane, it needs no weights, no GPU, and no host, and it is the artifact that converts HALT_NO_VALID_POINTING_SCALE from a dead end into a buildable scale.
required_properties: A malformed or unparseable model response must be counted, not dropped. Silent exclusion is the defect being fixed.
The denominator must be fixed and published before any model is run, and must include malformed responses as wrong.
The scorer must emit an overall score, or fail loud. It must never return successfully with no score.
The wrapper must record, for each item, whether it was parsed, malformed, or absent — three states, not two.
If wrapping requires changing PR-Bench's internals such that our number is no longer comparable to any published PR-Bench number, that must be stated in the output, not glossed.
phase_1_task.test_material: Synthetic and hand-written responses only. No model needs to be run to prove a scorer fails loud — construct the malformed cases directly.
acceptance: A pre-registered set of malformed inputs, each demonstrated to be counted rather than dropped.
A pre-registered set of well-formed inputs producing a score with an explicitly stated denominator.
One completely-returned run of the wrapper's own test set. An absence of visible errors is not acceptance.
A written statement of what the scale does NOT measure.
stop_conditions: If the strict wrapper cannot be built without making the number incomparable to published PR-Bench figures, STOP and report. That is a finding, not a failure.
If the scale turns out to require the opaque internal IDs that made the frozen visual family defective, STOP — the same defect must not be rebuilt.
If any step needs a GPU, a host, or a weight download, STOP and escalate. Do not proceed under an assumption.

required_correction.where: README.md line ~81: 'The parsed per-item rule matches the released PR-Bench evaluator.'
required_correction.problem: The module is stdlib-only. It does not call the released evaluator; it reimplements the rule from reading the released source. 'Matches' is an equivalence claim, and equivalence between two implementations is established by running both on the same inputs and comparing — not by reading one and writing the other, however carefully. Nothing in a synthetic self-test can establish it, because the released evaluator was never executed. The word 'wrapper' compounds this: it reads as 'we wrap the official code'.
required_correction.why_it_matters: This sentence is load-bearing. The entire per-category comparability story rests on it, and comparability is the only reason the number would mean anything to an outside reader.
required_correction.correct_predicate: Reimplements the released per-item rule as read from the released source. Equivalence to the released evaluator has NOT been established by execution.
required_correction.defect_class: Same shape as the recurring one: the artifact is genuine and careful, the predicate attached to it reaches past what was done. Correct it now, before it propagates into a downstream artifact.
required_correction.note: The lane's own hedges elsewhere are correct and should stay — per-category comparability conditioned on all-parsed and same data/coordinate conditions, and strict overall permanently marked a wrapper diagnostic that is never an official PR-Bench overall.

order: 2a. Real PR-Bench manifest + media. Downloads permitted under the gpu_packet download rules — domestic mirrors, sha256 and byte size recorded on arrival.

2b. DIFFERENTIAL TEST against the released evaluator. Run the released PR-Bench evaluator and this reimplementation on the same all-parsed inputs and compare per-item. This is the gate that converts the corrected predicate back into 'matches'. Until it passes, no comparability claim may be made against published PR-Bench figures.
2c. Incumbent baseline — the frozen Qwen3.8-27B on the real scale. See incumbent_premise_correction below.
